title: PayMe
tagline: Verified marketplace where creators earn when people or AI agents unlock their sources.
description:
PayMe is a marketplace for human-made knowledge in an AI-driven world. Creators can publish original articles, documents, transcripts, tutorials, skills, or research notes, then set a price for access. The app hashes each source to create a verifiable fingerprint, stores the full content behind a locked preview, and preserves the creator’s wallet-based attribution.

Readers or AI agents can browse sources, view previews for free, request a Hedera x402-style payment quote, and unlock the full content after payment verification. Each unlock records the buyer, creator, source, amount, currency, and transaction metadata, giving creators a basic earnings and usage history.

The goal is to create a simple payment and attribution layer for original human knowledge, so creators can prove ownership, control access, and get paid when their work is used by people or software agents.
how_its_made:
PayMe is built as a React + Vite frontend with a Python FastAPI backend. The frontend lets a creator enter a wallet-style identity, publish a source, browse the marketplace, preview locked content, request a payment quote, unlock a source, and test an AI-style citation flow.

The backend uses FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, and SQLite for the MVP data layer. When a source is created, the backend generates a SHA-256 content hash, stores the full content, creates a short preview, and exposes only the preview until the unlock endpoint verifies payment. Purchases are recorded with buyer wallet, creator wallet, amount, currency, and transaction metadata.

For Hedera, I implemented an x402-style exact-scheme payment quote using hedera:testnet, HBAR-to-tinybar conversion, a configurable pay-to account, and a verification layer with demo mode and strict mode. This makes each source unlock behave like a paid API request. I also added The Graph-ready analytics endpoints for marketplace stats and Bazantic-style manifest/recipe endpoints so agents can discover, unlock, and cite paid human-made sources. The hacky part is the demo verification mode, which lets the full product flow work locally before wiring in real facilitator settlement.
auto_summary: A React and FastAPI application for publishing paid knowledge sources with content previews, purchase records, and a Hedera-themed payment quote flow.
